Phase 1: Emergency Actions (Days 1-7)

⚠️ CRITICAL: All tasks in this section must be completed within 7 days. Incomplete remediation extends regulatory violation window.

Backend Team: Block PII Disclosure

Task 1: Restrict REST API User Endpoint

Priority: CRITICAL | Timeline: Days 1-3

Technical Description:

The endpoint /wp-json/wp/v2/users publicly exposes user information. Implement access restrictions immediately.

Solution: PHP Implementation
// Add to functions.php or custom plugin
add_filter('rest_endpoints', function($endpoints) {
    if (isset($endpoints['/wp/v2/users'])) {
        unset($endpoints['/wp/v2/users']);
    }
    return $endpoints;
});

// Alternative: Restrict by authorization
add_filter('rest_prepare_user', function($response, $user) {
    if (!current_user_can('list_users')) {
        return new WP_Error(
            'rest_forbidden',
            'Unauthorized access',
            ['status' => 403]
        );
    }
    return $response;
}, 10, 2);
Verification Checklist:
  • Test endpoint returns 403 Forbidden for anonymous users
  • Verify authenticated users with proper role can still access
  • Confirm no user details in JSON responses
  • Check logs for access attempts

Frontend Team: Deploy Content Security Policy

Task 2: Implement CSP Headers

Priority: HIGH | Timeline: Days 4-7

Technical Description:

Content Security Policy prevents XSS attacks by restricting resource loading. Deploy strict CSP configuration.

Solution: HTML Meta Tags
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="
  default-src 'self';
  script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' cdnjs.cloudflare.com;
  style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' fonts.googleapis.com;
  img-src 'self' data: https:;
  font-src 'self' fonts.gstatic.com;
  connect-src 'self';
  frame-ancestors 'none';
  upgrade-insecure-requests;
">
Verification Checklist:
  • Check browser console for CSP violation reports
  • Test script execution from external sources (should fail)
  • Verify inline scripts work without 'unsafe-inline'
  • Monitor CSP report-uri for violations

DevOps Team: Configure Security Headers

Task 3: Deploy HTTP Security Headers

Priority: HIGH | Timeline: Days 5-7

LiteSpeed Configuration (nginx-compatible):
server {
    add_header X-Frame-Options DENY;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff;
    add_header Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin;
    add_header Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()";
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload";
}
Apache Configuration:
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
    Header always set X-Frame-Options DENY
    Header always set X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
    Header always set Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin
    Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()"
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
</IfModule>
Verification Checklist:
  • Use curl to verify headers: curl -I https://example.com
  • Check browser DevTools Network tab for header presence
  • Test HSTS preload eligibility at https://hstspreload.org
  • Monitor error logs for configuration issues

Phase 2: Priority Implementation (Weeks 2-4)

Subresource Integrity (SRI) Implementation

Protect against compromised CDN resources by verifying content integrity.

Example: Cloudflare CDN with SRI
<link 
  rel="stylesheet" 
  href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/tailwindcss/3.0.0/tailwind.min.css"
  integrity="sha384-..." 
  crossorigin="anonymous"
>
<script 
  src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jquery/3.6.0/jquery.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-..." 
  crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

WordPress Component Updates

  • Update WordPress core to latest version
  • Update all active plugins (Blocksy, Stackable, LiteSpeed Cache)
  • Update PHP to 8.1+ (minimum 8.0)
  • Test updates on staging environment first

Incident Response Procedures

Level 1: Detection & Initial Response (First 15 Minutes)

  1. Alert Notification: Security team receives automated alert
  2. Initial Verification: Confirm incident type and severity
  3. Team Notification: Alert relevant technical teams
  4. Logging: Begin detailed incident logging

Level 2: Analysis & Containment (15 min - 2 hours)

  1. Root Cause Analysis: Identify attack vector and affected systems
  2. Containment Actions: Isolate affected components
  3. Business Impact Assessment: Evaluate customer and operational impact
  4. Communication Plan: Prepare stakeholder notifications

Level 3: Recovery & Post-Incident (2+ hours)

  1. System Recovery: Restore services from clean backups
  2. Evidence Preservation: Archive logs for forensic analysis
  3. Regulatory Notification: Notify authorities if required (GDPR: 72-hour window)
  4. Post-Mortem Review: Schedule security team debriefing

Weekly Security Procedures

Monday: Updates & Patching

  • Check WordPress security mailing list for new vulnerabilities
  • Review plugin update notifications
  • Test updates on development environment
  • Deploy patches to staging if available

Wednesday: Configuration Audit

  • Verify security headers are properly configured
  • Check firewall rules for unauthorized changes
  • Review access logs for suspicious activity
  • Test backup restoration procedures

Friday: Team Briefing

  • Security team meets with all technical teams
  • Review incidents from past week
  • Discuss any security alerts or concerns
  • Plan next week's security activities

Monthly Audit Procedures

Week 1: Access Control Review

  • Audit user access permissions across systems
  • Remove inactive user accounts (30+ days inactive)
  • Verify MFA is enabled for all admin accounts
  • Review recent privilege escalation events

Week 2: Vulnerability Assessment

  • Run automated security scanner (OWASP ZAP)
  • Compare results with previous month's findings
  • Document remediation status for known issues
  • Escalate new critical findings immediately

Week 3: Compliance Verification

  • Verify all security policies are followed
  • Check encryption for data in transit & at rest
  • Review incident response logs
  • Verify backup integrity and recoverability

Week 4: Planning & Training

  • Security team conducts staff training session
  • Review incident lessons learned
  • Plan next month's security initiatives
  • Generate compliance report for management

Monitoring & Detection Setup

Essential Monitoring:

  • Web Application Firewall (WAF): Monitor Cloudflare logs for blocked requests
  • Access Logs: Track unusual access patterns to sensitive endpoints
  • Error Logs: Monitor PHP/web server error rates
  • System Resources: CPU, memory, disk usage alerts

Advanced Monitoring (Recommended):

  • SIEM Platform: Centralized log analysis and alerting
  • Intrusion Detection (IDS): Network-level threat detection
  • File Integrity Monitoring (FIM): Detect unauthorized file changes
  • Database Activity Monitoring: Track suspicious database queries

Quick Action Summary

Complete Before End of Week 1:

  1. Block REST API user endpoint (Backend Team)
  2. Deploy CSP headers (Frontend Team)
  3. Configure security headers (DevOps Team)
  4. Conduct team verification testing

Complete During Weeks 2-4:

  1. Implement Subresource Integrity for all CDN resources
  2. Update all WordPress components
  3. Establish weekly security review procedures
  4. Deploy continuous monitoring solution
